intake: believer - lifelong active Latter-day Saint, temple recommend, believe in a personal embodied Heavenly Father who answers prayer and in a literal resurrection; I know I am the kind of man a good sentence can carry, so I tried to read slow.

walk.note: That is how it came to me as a boy, through my parents' story, even if I'd say the Spirit confirmed it later rather than a 'need' driving it.

I grant I can't put the First Vision or my own witness in a lab, and I grant men wrote the scriptures; it does not follow that God's word can't come through men's hands, nor that the next stop must be Aquinas's God who is 'being itself' rather than a Father.
The dilemma is a good one, but a God who chooses to be seen by some and not others is exactly a person; the right conclusion is that the classical conception is wrong, not that God is doubtful.

The STEP study stings a little, I'll admit it, but prayer was never 'outcomes should line up'; it is 'Thy will be done,' and a God who veils Himself to leave us our agency is choosing, which I am happy to say.
Granting there is no God, the mind still does not look to me like something a pile of chemistry just does; though my own church teaches spirit is a finer kind of matter, so I hold 'dualism' loosely.
I watched my mother-in-law's dementia and I know mind leans on brain while we live, but that the instrument fails does not show there was no player; a broken radio proves nothing about the station.
Fair enough; 'matter' is too narrow, and oddly that is closer to what Joseph Smith said about spirit than the author may know.
That physics describes structure and not what has it does not make the world a dream; the frost kills the alfalfa whether anyone is dreaming it or not.
If it is a dream, somebody is dreaming it; I'll take that even with Lichtenberg's warning.
'The problem begins with I, and then necessarily You' - I noticed that one moved me and checked it, and it still holds.
I take it gladly, though I would say charity was commanded of me and I also chose it, and I don't see why those can't both be true.
'We see through a glass, darkly' is learned ignorance, and I know that country.

Faith held knowingly after sixty-nine years is a fair description of mine; and 'a system that carries what others cannot, at a cost to itself' is the Atonement without the name, which is partly why I am suspicious of how much I liked it.
Hoping toward a Maker does not require Him to be a finished, motionless mind; the author concedes as much in the last sentence, and my Father remembers, works, and weeps.
A bargain between whom, over what? There is nothing on the page for me to take or refuse.

'To think is to ignore for any possible mind' is a claim about God made from inside a human skull; the hairs of my head are numbered, and the author herself says Aquinas's way of knowing hasn't been shown incoherent.
Granting no Maker, suffering is still bad for the one who suffers; and I never believed good was good only because God said so, so this costs me less than the author may expect.
Yes, if the good is in beings then whether each one continues matters and something has to carry it; I just think the map already met the One who carries it at move 13 and sent Him away at move 16.
I would not sit at the edge waiting for a machine to tell me whether the outside can prove the inside; I'd say it can't, and that is what faith was for all along.

first_exit.why: I can grant that nothing I have is verifiable to a stranger and that men held the pen, but the step from there to 'evidence must lie outside the texts' and then to Aquinas's God skips the possibility I actually live by: that God speaks through men and confirms it to the reader, and that He is a Person, not being itself.

comment: At move 13 you wrote down the Atonement without naming it - one who bears a cost for those with no claim on it, so the good can go on - and then at move 16 you ruled out the only Being who ever claimed to have done it, on a premise you admit you have not proved. I have buried enough people to know that being remembered by others is not the hope that got me out of bed the morning after, and I don't believe it is yours either, or you would have stopped walking sooner. Look again at whether 'to think is to ignore' is something you know or something you would rather were true.
